 Hannah Postlethwait is an author and entertainment journalist living in Iowa. A lifelong writer, Hannah refined her skills at Iowa State University, graduating with degrees in journalism and American Indian Studies, which catalyzed her passion for empowering diversity representation in mass media.
Hannah wrote her debut novel after graduating, which probes the future of AI integration and its ingraining effects on the human experience. During that time, Hannah worked in commerce, healthcare, and marketing to deepen her understanding of the human condition and the marketplace.
After completing her book, Hannah returned to journalism and features writing, landing a position at ScreenRant that led to her role at CBR. As a senior writer for the site, Hannah covers the latest in television and streaming, specializing in the network TV cycle.
Hannah is drawn to the complexities of formatting a television narrative and is fascinated by the industry's successes and failures. Her current work expands her understanding of what makes a series memorable, research she uses to craft her own stories.

 The following contains spoilers for Chicago PD Season 14. 
 Until Kevin Atwater’s (LaRoyce Hawkins) exit in Chicago PD Season 14, Episode 2, every main character introduced in Season 1 left under a dark cloud. Atwater is the first to ride off into the sunset, a rarity for the series as Dick Wolf’s One Chicago universe navigates a couple of original-character exits in NBC’s 2026-2027 broadcast slate.

 Across the franchise, two original series characters are departing. Along with Atwater on Chicago PD, Joe Cruz (Joe Miñoso) exits Chicago Fire with an emotional, family-driven sendoff. That said, One Chicago is navigating massive changes this fall as it returns to NBC Wednesday nights with new episodes, especially as Chicago PD flips the script for Atwater.
 Darkness Clouds Chicago PD's Major Season 1 Character Exits
 The main characters introduced in Season 1 and their departures reveal Chicago PD 's dark history. They include Hank Voight (Jason Beghe), Antonio Dawson (Jon Seda), Erin Lindsay (Sophia Bush), Jay Halstead (Jesse Lee Soffer), Adam Ruzek (Patrick John Flueger), Sheldon Jin (Archie Kao), Alvin Olinsky (Elias Koteas), Kim Burgess (Marina Squerciati), Trudy Platt (Amy Morton), and Atwater.
 That said, Platt and Atwater were recurring characters in Chicago PD Season 1, not main cast members. Still, they were both bumped up to series regulars at the start of Season 2, making them just as pivotal to the series as Season 1's main cast. So, where other recurring characters fell off, both Platt and Atwater have become staples.
 After Atwater’s exit in Chicago PD Season 14, the four main characters introduced in Season 1 who remain are Voight, Ruzek, Platt, and Burgess. Notwithstanding Atwater’s departure, every character’s exit is marked by death, tragedy, or misconduct, starting with Jin’s death in Chicago PD Season 1’s finale, when his throat is slit to tie up loose ends after he’s blackmailed.
 Lindsay is next to leave, hesitantly taking an FBI job in New York at the end of Chicago PD Season 4 after she uses excessive force on a suspect and is facing an Internal Affairs investigation. Olinsky’s exit is even worse, stabbed to death in prison in Season 5 after taking the fall for a murder that Voight committed.
 In Chicago PD Season 6, Dawson relapses on painkillers, causing him to spiral and leave the team. Halstead resigns a few years later in Season 10, walking away from the unit and his wife, Hailey Upton (Tracy Spiridakos), and leaving for Bolivia after becoming disillusioned with the gray area of his intelligence work, cementing a clouded history.
 Chicago PD’s Showrunner Fought For Atwater’s Happy Ending
 That’s where Atwater’s exit sets itself apart: he chooses a stable life for his new family and leaves the show on his own terms in Chicago PD Season 14. Atwater even receives Voight’s blessing, marking the first time an original character from Season 1 has received this kind of farewell, unclouded by death or wrongdoing.
 Atwater’s story is one fans can look back on and smile about. After he and his partner, Tasha Fox (Karen Obilom), welcome a son, Atwater is inspired to change course when he's shot in his bulletproof vest, which pushes him toward a teaching position at the police academy in Atlanta, where he can prioritize his safety for baby Malcolm.
 Atwater undoubtedly gets a proper police procedural sendoff, gathering with Tasha and the rest of the team at Molly’s for celebratory drinks before he departs. Atwater gives a farewell speech, raising a toast to the entire 21st District Intelligence Unit while expressing his gratitude before he is sent off with a rendition of For He's a Jolly Good Fellow. 
 Chicago PD showrunner Gwen Sigan felt it was important to see Atwater off in a positive light. “We wanted to give that character a sendoff that he deserves and something his character has earned and make it positive, in a way, for him,” she said in an interview, noting it was a “rarity” for the darkest One Chicago show.
 After Atwater’s departure, a recruit named Donovan “Penny” Watts (Naiqui Macabroad) has replaced the empty seat in the intelligence unit. In Chicago PD Season 14, Episode 4, Voight recruits him after the 11th District beat cop assists in their investigation. That said, Penny sets the tone for the season, as Voight seeks out an officer who’s impulsive and headstrong.
